Upon graduation, students in the Secondary Education Program obtain certification to teach at the High School level (grades 7-12).

The new program proposal is intended address the changes in Rhode Island certification regulations, which will require significant changes (over 25%) to the requirements for our current BA in Secondary Education with a specialization in World Languages, effectively transforming it into a BA in World Language Education -All Grades.

In the proposed new program, students will take a variety of existing EDC courses in Elementary Education, Early Childhood Education, Secondary Education, and Teaching English as a Second Language / Bilingual Education concentrations so that, upon graduation, they will be more versatile and highly employable educators who are better prepared to teach effectively in a wider variety of educational settings.
The financial cost to the university of this new program will be zero, as our students will be required to take existing courses that are regularly offered in the School o f Education.
The development of new courses will not be necessary to implement the proposed overhaul of the program.

Course Approval Process

The Course/Program Approval Process at URI 1.
Initial Submission on Kuali.
Faculty members submit course (for both new and modified classes) and program proposals within Kuali Curriculum Management.
Kuali provides workflow at URI for curricular changes and is in the university’s Microsoft 365 suite; further information and login link can be found here: https://web.uri.edu/facsen/kuali/.
A library impact statement will be generated for new courses within one week of submission to Kuali.
Crosslisted classes, courses/programs that might overlap with existing offerings, and classes/programs assuming prerequisites from other departments need to provide documentation regarding approval from those other relevant academic units.
New programs need to allow two weeks for a Budget Impact Statement to be completed by the Budget Office.
Note: new programs must also complete the New Program Assessment Plan (https://web.uri.edu/atl/assessment/newprograms/) and submit it to the Assessment Team at assess@uri.edu. 2.
Approval Requirements.

Once a faculty member submits a new course proposal, either the department’s curriculum committee or the department chair/program head must approve it based on the governance structure of the department.
This approval requires a vote of the faculty of the originating department.
Courses not originating within a specific department or college must be approved by the governing committee responsible for administering the program.
As part of their approval, the departmental curriculum committee or chairs/program heads must submit an official statement confirming departmental approval via faculty vote for the proposal. 3.
College-level Review.
After approval by the department, the proposal is reviewed for approval by the college curriculum committee(s), and then approved by the college dean or delegate.
Colleges assess course proposals for issues such as staffing, intra-college departmental and interdepartmental overlap, and collegewide programmatic needs and requirements. 4.
Senate Committee Review.
After college-level approval, proposals go to the Faculty Senate Specialist who formats and prepares them for the following month’s curriculum committee meetings.

Course/program proposals are directed to the appropriate Senate Committee(s): undergraduate General Education courses to the General Education Committee (GEC); all other undergraduate courses/programs to the Curriculum and Standards Committee (CASC); graduate courses/programs to the Graduate Council (GC).
These committees examine proposals with an eye to legibility and benefit to students. 5.
Full Senate Review.
The GEC, CASC, and the GC each make monthly reports to the entire Faculty Senate.
During these reports, they bring forward all new course/program proposals approved at the committee-level for a vote by the entire Senate.
Courses approved by this vote are then added to a bill for signature by the Faculty Senate President.
The President/Provost then provides final signature approval.
Concerns covered at this level typically include unexpected impacts on other programs or lack of resources.
Please note: 400 level courses proposed for graduate credit need to be approved by both the undergraduate and graduate committees within the department and college; at the Faculty Senate level, these proposals go before both the GC and CASC.

Please also note: courses are not approved for an immediate change; after completion of the approval process, they only become active in the term and year indicated in the proposal.
A complete proposal approved by each of the necessary levels might move through the process in 2-3 months.
Faculty submitting course proposals should carefully consult the meeting schedules for their college-level curriculum committee(s); the GEC, CASC, and GC; and the Faculty Senate itself.
They should also watch for notifications from Kuali if one of these bodies needs more information.
